summary: Accepted the beneficiary relationship from the lithium cycle to Lithium Americas with high positive project sensitivity and medium confidence. Current SEC-filed Q1 2026 evidence supports a direct path from lithium demand and pricing through Thacker Pass economics, funding, offtake, and project option value, while 62% ownership, remaining capex, DOE and GM terms, warrants, dilution, schedule, commissioning, and unsupported common-equity valuation remain explicit limits. Updated the relationship page, catalog, log, and canonical relationship row; no strategy or follow-up operation was created.

evidence.claim: Lithium Americas' SEC-filed Q1 2026 Form 10-Q reports USD 758.5 million cash and USD 449.1 million restricted cash at 31 March 2026, USD 1.1 billion spent against the technical report's USD 2.93 billion Phase 1 capex estimate, fiscal-2026 project capex guidance of USD 1.3-1.6 billion, late-2027 targeted mechanical completion, and a planned 2028 production ramp. These facts establish concentrated development-stage lithium exposure while preserving construction, funding, schedule, and pre-revenue risk.

The maintained security review confirms Lithium Americas' 62% Thacker Pass ownership, GM joint-venture and offtake exposure, DOE conditions, warrants, observed ATM dilution, pre-revenue status, and an ineligible low-confidence assessment with valuation_unsupported because project economics cannot yet be reconciled to common-share value.

The maintained idea defines the causal channel from EV and stationary-storage demand plus delayed supply to lithium pricing and funded-project option value, while preserving supply restarts, recycling, sodium-ion substitution, capital intensity, funding, dilution, and commissioning as contrary evidence.
